On October 28, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that attackers were exploiting the two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws let anyone execute code on the web server without authentication. The disclosure itself went a little wrong.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-104883 - Contao Privilege Escalation via Theme Import Capability
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-104883
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 11:45 p.m. | 1 hour, 6 minutes ago
  
Description :Commit `2b83a60f7763` (5.7.3) hardened the template editor: it added `TemplateEditorModuleVoter` + `CheckTemplateEditorSaveListener` so a non-admin cannot self-grant the `tpl_editor` backend module (editable PHP-capable templates permit server-side code execution). That voter supports only the `modules` field and the literal value `tpl_editor`.

The equally RCE-capable `theme_import` capability lives in a different field - the `themes` checkbox field (tl_user_group.php:98-105 options include `theme_import`; identical on tl_user.php:248-253) - which has no save_callback and no voter. `TemplateEditorModuleVoter` is the only DC voter registered for tl_user_group, and it does not cover the `themes` field. So a delegated user manager can add `theme_import` to their own (or a managed) account.

Live repro (Contao 5.7.9):
1. As admin, create a non-admin backend group with the `user` (or `group`) module (a delegated user manager), and a user in it. Confirm the user cannot access `tpl_editor` (blocked by the 5.7.3 voter).
2. As that non-admin, edit a group/account: add `themes` to the modules field and `theme_import` to the themes field (both accepted - only `tpl_editor` is blocked). Re-authenticate.

## Impact

A delegated user/group manager (a role explicitly not trusted with template/code access) escalates to arbitrary PHP execution on the server, fully compromising the installation. This bypasses the exact protection the 5.7.3 `tpl_editor` fix introduced.

## Credits

This security vulnerability was found by @HDWSec
  
Severity: 7.2 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 7:18 p.m. | 41 minutes ago
  
Description :NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. vulnerability.summary:

Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 5:40 p.m. | 19 minutes ago
  
Description :LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the authenticated GET /lists/{list}/feed and GET /tags/{tag}/feed handlers in app/Http/Controllers/App/FeedController.php use integer route model binding without an object-level authorization or visibility check. vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-103933
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 5:30 p.m. | 29 minutes ago
  
Description :Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 2.1.0 until 4.5.2, get_eacontent in libatalk/vfs/ea_ad.c subtracts MAX_REPLY_EXTRA_BYTES from a client-controlled FPGetExtAttr MaxReplySize without rejecting values from 1 through 5, and a signed-to-unsigned comparison can then select an untrusted AppleDouble ea_size. An authenticated client on a volume configured with ea = ad can use a pre-existing malformed AppleDouble sidecar to make read copy attacker-controlled bytes beyond dsi->data + 6 into the surrounding struct DSI, including protocol callback pointers. The malformed sidecar must already exist or be created through a separate local, co-export, management, restore, or vulnerability-assisted write path, and practical code execution depends on the target architecture, structure layout, and address uncertainty; runtime command execution was demonstrated on one x86-64 build. Volumes using ea = sys, ea = none, or ea = auto when it resolves to native system xattrs do not reach this path. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-95824 - Infinite loop in IPv6 Router Advertisement handling when the RA omits the source link-layer address option
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-95824
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 5:18 p.m. | 41 minutes ago
  
Description :The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery code in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c flushes a neighbour's queued packets at the end of handle_ra_input(). The Source Link-Layer Address Option (SLLAO) is optional in a Router Advertisement; when it is absent, handle_ra_input() still obtains (or creates) a neighbour cache entry for the RA source via net_ipv6_nbr_add() with a NULL link-layer address, so the entry stays in NET_IPV6_NBR_STATE_INCOMPLETE with nbr->idx == NET_NBR_LLADDR_UNKNOWN. The pending-packet drain loop was entered unconditionally for that unresolved entry.

Each net_send_data() in the drain loop runs synchronously into net_ipv6_prepare_for_send(), which finds the neighbour still unresolved and hands the packet to net_ipv6_send_ns(), which puts it straight back onto the same pending_queue. The loop therefore never sees an empty queue. With a single queued packet it transmits a fresh Neighbor Solicitation on every iteration; with two or more queued packets it rotates the queue with no allocation and no transmission at all. The loop runs in the network RX thread with the global IPv6 neighbour mutex held.

An unauthenticated attacker on the same link can trigger this deterministically: advertise itself as a router, induce the victim to queue off-link traffic toward that router (for example by sending echo requests with an off-link source address) while leaving the solicitation unanswered, then send a second Router Advertisement without an SLLAO option. Spoofing an SLLAO-less RA from the legitimate router's link-local address has the same effect whenever traffic is queued for it. Router Advertisements are processed with no authentication whenever CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ND is enabled, which is the default for IPv6-capable builds.

The result is a permanent denial of service: the RX thread spins forever holding the neighbour lock, so all IPv6 transmission and every other user of the neighbour cache blocks, and the Neighbor Advertisement that would resolve the entry can no longer be processed. The ipv6_ns_reply_timer work item that would normally drop the pending packets also blocks on the same mutex. In the single-packet variant the loop additionally floods the link with Neighbor Solicitations. The fix restricts the flush to resolved entries (nbr->idx != NET_NBR_LLADDR_UNKNOWN), leaving the packets queued for the NS reply timeout. There is no memory-safety impact.
  
Severity: 6.5 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-79751 - SportEase profile update permits class representative self-assignment through user-controlled class_id
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-79751
  
Published : 20 de Novembro de 2026 às 17:18 | 28 minutos ago
  
Description :SportEase is a web application for managing school sports events, class rosters, and competition teams. Prior to 1.3, an authenticated account with is_profile_complete=false can submit an attacker-selected class_id for any class in the currently active event to PUT /api/user/profile during first profile completion. AuthHandler.UpdateProfile accepts the class without validating the user's legitimate membership and automatically derives and assigns the corresponding {class_name}_rep role while isFirstCompletion is true. The attacker can become representative of one selected class, view roster information including email addresses, and add or remove competition-team assignments. Downstream handlers correctly reject access to other classes, so the impact is bounded to the selected class, but the representative privilege cannot be revoked through the exposed API and requires direct database intervention or another out-of-band remediation method. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.
  
Severity: 7.6 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-122244 - Budibase: Cross-privilege Stored XSS in the Budibase Builder via broken HTML-escaping in `jsonFormatter.format()` rendered through `{@html}` in the CSP-less Builder origin
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-122244
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 4:50 p.m. | 24 minutes ago
  
Description :Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, a BASIC application user, or an unauthenticated visitor to a public write form, can store markup in a shared external datasource that a builder or administrator later evaluates in any Handlebars binding Preview that surfaces the value, including the Data-section Formula column editor or any binding drawer. jsonFormatter.format() in packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts leaves raw strings and object keys unescaped, while packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte inserts the formatted result as raw HTML. The Handlebars SafeString path preserves the attacker-controlled value, and the Builder origin lacks a Content-Security-Policy that would block the resulting script. This permits stored script execution in the higher-privileged builder or administrator session rather than the writer's own role, allowing privileged Builder API actions and workspace data access. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133850 - flowintel: Stale Authorization Allows Notification Disclosure After Case Access Revocation
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133850
  
Published : 20 de Novembro de 2026 às 15:17 | 29 minutos ago
  
Description :flowintel contains an authorization flaw in its recurring reminder notification subsystem. When a user is subscribed to recurring notifications for a case, the system does not re-verify the recipient's current access rights to that case before generating or displaying the notification.

As a result, a user who previously had access to a private case and later had that access revoked can still:
- Receive recurring reminder notifications containing case-related content.
- View stored reminder notifications in their notification list, including notification counts, even though they no longer have permission to view the underlying case.

The vulnerability affects both the notification creation path (recurring reminder generation) and the notification display path (listing and counting stored reminders). The issue arises because the authorization check performed at subscription time is not re-applied at delivery or retrieval time.

Security impact is limited to information disclosure: an unauthorized user may observe case titles, reminder messages, and associated metadata that they no longer have permission to access. No integrity or availability impact is indicated by the patch.

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
  
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133853 - FlowIntel Chatbot Shared MCP Session Allows Cross-User API Identity Confusion
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133853
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 3:17 p.m. | 41 minutes ago
  
Description :FlowIntel's chatbot component used a single shared MCP (Model Context Protocol) session and process-wide environment variable to pass per-user API credentials to a child process. Because the session and the ambient FLOWINTEL_API_KEY environment variable were shared across all concurrent requests, a user's authenticated identity could be applied to another user's tool invocation, or a stale/ambient credential could be inherited by a new request.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with access to the chatbot interface.
- Concurrent or overlapping chatbot tool invocations from different users, or a request made after another user's credentials were written to the process environment.

Impact:
- A lower-privilege user could read data belonging to a higher-privilege user (e.g., private investigation cases).
- A user whose session was invalidated (deleted, password changed, key revoked) could still operate under a previously cached ambient credential.

vulnerability.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
vulnerability.summary:
CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

CVE-2025-42884 SAP NetWeaver Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic Vulnerability
CVE-2026-76466 Cisco Expressway Series Use of Hard-coded Credentials Vulnerability
CVE-2026-123890 VMWare vCenter Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability
CVE-2026-129448 Apache Roller Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. 
Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. 


While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. 


Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133667 - flowintel DOM-based XSS via Timeline Autolinking, Search Highlighting, and Content-Type Confusion
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133667
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 11:18 a.m. | 18 minutes ago
  
Description :flowintel contains multiple related flaws that allow an authenticated attacker to inject arbitrary HTML or script into pages viewed by other users.

- Timeline rendering: the timeline library's autolinking feature rewrote already-sanitised case notes and imported MISP attribute values into generated HTML link elements. Crafted text containing quote characters could break out of the generated attribute context, altering the surrounding markup and enabling script execution in the victim's browser.

- Search highlighting: the highlight injection logic used a regular expression to locate text between angle brackets and spliced  elements into the resulting string. Because the pattern could match inside HTML attribute values, the rewrite could corrupt or inject content into attributes of already-sanitised markup, again leading to DOM-based cross-site scripting.

- Content-Type confusion: three analyser selection endpoints returned session-stored JSON strings with a text/html content type. A browser receiving such a response will parse and render the body as HTML, so any HTML or script embedded in the stored value is executed in the victim's context.

Preconditions: the attacker must be an authenticated user with the ability to create or import case content (notes, MISP attributes) containing specially crafted quote or angle-bracket sequences. The victim must subsequently open the affected case timeline, run a search, or request one of the selection endpoints.

Impact: successful exploitation yields DOM-based cross-site scripting in the victim's browser session, potentially allowing disclosure of case data, session manipulation, or execution of arbitrary actions under the victim's identity.

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
  
Severity: 4.8 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133661 - FlowIntel: Missing Authorization and Credential Scope Enforcement in Connector and Template Features
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133661
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 11:18 a.m. | 18 minutes ago
  
Description :FlowIntel contains multiple authorization and credential management vulnerabilities affecting connector instances, MISP helper tools, and case templates.

- Connector instance metadata, connectivity checks, and case listings accepted instance IDs without verifying if the acting user had visibility or ownership rights, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive configuration and data.
- Case template serialization and creation processes exposed connector instances attached to templates regardless of the user's permissions, potentially leaking credentials or instance details to users who should not have access.
- Editing connector instances allowed changes to URLs or sharing scopes without requiring re-authentication of API keys, enabling the reuse of another user's credentials in a new context or the leakage of shared keys to unauthorized endpoints.
- Outbound MISP connector keys were incorrectly accepted for authenticating incoming alerts, bypassing the intended separation between outbound integration credentials and inbound alert source authentication.

These issues allow authenticated users to access unauthorized connector data, manipulate credential scopes, and potentially exploit credential confusion between different security contexts.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133652 - Flowintel Session Identifiers Not Bound to Credentials Allow Persistent Access After Password Change
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133652
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 11:18 a.m. | 18 minutes ago
  
Description :Flowintel , contained a session management vulnerability in its browser authentication mechanism. The session identifier used a bare numeric user ID rather than a credential-bound token, resulting in several related weaknesses:

- Remembered logins (remember-me cookies) remained valid after a user changed their password, allowing an attacker holding a previously issued cookie to retain access indefinitely.
- Server-side session identifiers were not rotated upon login (local, SSO, or remembered), enabling session fixation.
- Self-service email and password changes did not require verification of the current password, permitting an attacker with an active session to modify account credentials without knowledge of the existing password.
- Administrator-initiated password resets did not revoke other browser sessions, invalidate remembered logins, or rotate the affected user's API key.

An attacker who obtained a valid session or remember-me cookie (e.g., through XSS, network interception, or cookie theft) could maintain unauthorized access even after the legitimate user changed their password. Additionally, an attacker with any valid session could change the account's email address or password without knowing the current credentials, effectively taking over the account.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
  
Severity: 7.2 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-115409 - Unverified key-pair binding lets an unauthenticated token user substitute the public key or certificate returned for a private key
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-115409
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 9:33 a.m. | 50 minutes ago
  
Description :In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `<= 2.0.0-rc8` (and the deprecated v1 module paths `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11 <= 1.6.8`, `github.com/ThalesGroup/crypto11 <= 1.7.0-rc1` and `github.com/ThalesIgnite/crypto11 <= 1.2.5`), the key-pair and certificate lookup functions (`FindKeyPair`, `FindKeyPairs`, `FindKeyPairsWithAttributes`, `FindAllKeyPairs`, the `FindRSAKeyPair*` family and `FindAllPairedCertificates`) pair a private key with a public key object, or with a certificate, by `CKA_ID`/`CKA_LABEL` alone, take the first match the token returns, and never verify that it belongs to the private key. PKCS#11 permits a session that has not logged in to create public token objects, so anyone able to open a session on the token — without the PIN — can plant a public key or certificate carrying a victim key's `CKA_ID` and label, and crypto11 may return it as that key's public half. An application that publishes or trusts `Signer.Public()` (a JWKS endpoint, a key registry, `authorized_keys`, a CSR) then publishes the attacker's key, and relying parties accept anything the attacker signs as coming from the service. On the v1 line the lookup also falls back to a class-and-key-type-only search when the private key has no `CKA_ID`, pairing a label-only private key with the first public key of its type on the token.



The v1 module paths are deprecated and will not be fixed; users should migrate to github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2 version 2.0.0-rc9 or later.
  
Severity: 6.5 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133627 - flowintel Case History Log Injection via Line Separator Characters in User-Authored Fields
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133627
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 8:52 a.m. | 11 minutes ago
  
Description :flowintel contains a log injection vulnerability in its case history (audit log) subsystem. The case history is stored as a line-delimited file where each line represents a single event attributed to a specific user. User-controlled fields, including user names, event messages, and case titles used during case merging, were written to the history file without sanitizing embedded line separator characters (such as carriage return, line feed, vertical tab, form feed, and Unicode line/paragraph separators).

An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify case history entries could embed line separators in these fields. Upon writing, the injected separators would split a single intended entry into multiple lines, each of which the history format interprets as a distinct event. This allows an attacker to forge additional history entries attributed to arbitrary users, corrupting the audit trail and undermining the integrity of case records.

The vulnerability affects the case history append and merge operations. No authentication bypass or privilege escalation is required beyond normal case-management access.

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
  
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133613 - Flowintel Community Data Launcher Exposes Admin API Key in Child Process Arguments
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133613
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 7:38 a.m. | 20 minutes ago
  
Description :Flowintel's community data launcher script passes the admin API key as a command-line argument to a child Python helper process. On Unix-like systems, process arguments are readable by all local users via standard tools such as ps or by reading /proc//cmdline, allowing any local user to observe the key while the helper process is running.

An attacker with local access to the host can capture the admin API key during the brief window in which the helper process is active. Possession of the key grants full administrative access to the Flowintel REST API, enabling unauthorized creation, modification, or deletion of threat intelligence data, users, roles, and organisations.

Preconditions:
- The victim must invoke the community data import or deletion command (launch.sh -tdc or -dtdc) with the API key supplied as a positional argument.
- The attacker must have a local user account on the same host and be able to observe process listings during the helper execution window.

Impact:
- Disclosure of the Flowintel admin API key to any local user.
- Subsequent full administrative control over the Flowintel instance via its REST API.

Affected: <4.1.0
  
Severity: 6.4 | MEDIUM

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133422 - Quadratic time unique_items list validation in Pydantic V1
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133422
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 7:33 a.m. | 24 minutes ago
  
Description :Validating an untrusted list into a field constrained with unique_items=True with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few hundred kilobytes takes seconds to validate.

The ConstrainedList.unique_items_validator validator (in pydantic/types.py) checks each item against all the following ones. For a list with no duplicates (the common, valid case), this results in a quadratic number of comparisons.

The issue was fixed in commit 6ec75e57f277a820ec583e601167f25fe8dc7c87. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted lists into fields constrained with unique_items=True (using conlist() or Field()).

The fix only applies to lists of builtin scalar types (int, float, str, bytes, bool and None), for which duplicates can be detected in linear time. Lists of other types (e.g. models or dictionaries) are still checked in quadratic time, as their items aren't guaranteed to be hashable: bound their size using the max_items constraint.

Pydantic V2 models are not affected.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133611 - vulnerability-lookup: 2FA Disabled via Unauthenticated GET Request and Unpublished Comments Accessible Without Authorization
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133611
  
Published : 2026年11月20日 07:17 | 14 分钟 ago
  
Description :vulnerability-lookup prior to version 7.1.0 contains two security issues in its web interface. First, the /user/toggle_2fa endpoint accepted HTTP GET requests and disabled the authenticated user's two-factor authentication without requiring password confirmation. Because the state-changing operation was reachable via GET, an attacker with a basic account could embed an image element (or any other GET-triggering markup) in a comment pointing to that endpoint. When a victim with 2FA enabled viewed the comment, their browser silently issued the GET request, disabling the victim's second factor of authentication. No CSRF token was enforced on the GET path, and no password was required to confirm the action. Second, the comment detail page (/comment/) rendered unpublished comments to any visitor who possessed the URL, bypassing the moderation workflow that was intended to keep such content hidden until approved. The API correctly restricted access, but the web view did not enforce the same authorization check. The combined effect allows an attacker to degrade a victim's account security (removal of 2FA) through a single page view and to read content that was not yet approved for public release.
  
Severity: 4.6 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99803 - io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate()
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99803
  
Published : 2026年11月20日 07:02 | 29 分钟 ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate()

When an IORING_OP_SOCKET request is prepared in io_socket_prep(),
sock->type retains creation flags such as SOCK_CLOEXEC and SOCK_NONBLOCK
until __sys_socket_file() masks them off with SOCK_TYPE_MASK during
execution.

However, io_socket_bpf_populate() copies sock->type into
bctx->socket.type without masking off ~SOCK_TYPE_MASK. As a result, a
cBPF filter inspecting bctx->socket.type against socket types such as
SOCK_DGRAM or SOCK_STREAM can be bypassed by ORing SOCK_CLOEXEC or
SOCK_NONBLOCK into the socket type.

Mask sock->type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK when populating bctx->socket.type.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99795 - cxl/features: Ensure that count is set before access to ent[] __counted_by()
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99795
  
Published : 2026年11月20日 06:18 | 44 分钟 ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cxl/features: Ensure that count is set before access to ent[] __counted_by()

get_supported_features() assigns entries->num_features only after the
memcpy() loop that fills entries->ent[] has already run. Since ent[]
is __counted_by(num_features), the compiler's bounds instrumentation
sees a 0-length array during that loop and FORTIFY_SOURCE trips on
the memcpy. Set @num_features right after allocation, before any
write into ent[], so the bound is correct for the whole lifetime of
the array.

This was found via a fortify panic:

 memcpy: detected buffer overflow: 384 byte write of buffer size 0
 WARNING: lib/string_helpers.c:1035 at __fortify_report+0x54/0xa0
 kernel BUG at lib/string_helpers.c:1043!
 Call trace:
  __fortify_panic+0x10/0x18
  get_supported_features.isra.0+0x4a0/0x4d0 [cxl_core]
  devm_cxl_setup_features+0x84/0x120 [cxl_core]
  cxl_pci_probe+0x254/0x5e0 [cxl_pci]

Same class of bug, same fix shape as commit 6c9d2e87df40
("cxl/fwctl: Fix __fortify_panic"), which fixed the analogous issue
in cxlctl_get_supported_features() but missed this one.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99788 - ACPI: CPPC: Validate FFH register fields before hardware access
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99788
  
Published : 2026年11月20日 06:18 | 44 分钟 ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ACPI: CPPC: Validate FFH register fields before hardware access

The x86 CPPC FFH accessors construct masks and shift values using the
firmware's Bit Width and Bit Offset without checking that the field fits
in an MSR. A zero-width field or a field extending beyond bit 63 can
therefore cause an invalid shift. The safe MSR accessors only handle an
access fault, not invalid field arithmetic after a successful read.

Also, the 64-bit GAS address is implicitly narrowed to the 32-bit MSR
number. A descriptor with nonzero upper address bits can access a different
MSR from the one described by firmware.

The arm64 AMU counter readers have the same unchecked field arithmetic.
Validate the field bounds before reading a counter, including both
descriptors in the paired counter path.

Dispatch FFH accesses before decoding the GAS Access Size in the common
read and write paths. Otherwise, a large access_width can trigger an
invalid shift in GET_BIT_WIDTH() before the architecture validates its
register. That field has architecture-specific FFH semantics and is not
needed by the generic memory/port accessor on this path.

Validate x86 MSR addresses and share the field-bounds checks between
related accessors within each architecture.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99787 - cpufreq: CPPC: Select the frequency-invariance callback per CPU
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99787
  
Published : 2026年11月20日 06:18 | 44 分钟 ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cpufreq: CPPC: Select the frequency-invariance callback per CPU

cppc_cpufreq_cpu_fie_init() initializes deferred work only for CPUs whose
feedback counters use PCC. However, if any CPU in a shared policy uses PCC,
it installs the PCC tick callback for the entire policy. With FIE enabled,
a non-PCC CPU then queues an uninitialized irq_work and can call a NULL
function pointer when that work runs.

Choose the frequency-invariance callback separately for each CPU using
the recorded work-initialization state. Processor removal can unpublish
the CPC descriptor before callback registration, so querying its counter
transport again can incorrectly select direct reads for a PCC CPU.

Register the callbacks after all counter initialization has completed, so
a failed initial read for an online CPU cannot leave a partially
registered policy. PCC CPUs use their initialized deferred work, while
non-PCC CPUs read their own counters directly from the tick.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99792 - smb/server: prevent file publication after tree disconnect
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99792
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 5:51 a.m. | 31 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb/server: prevent file publication after tree disconnect

TREE_DISCONNECT closes the tree's published file handles before marking and
removing the tree connection. A concurrent CREATE that already holds a tree
reference can therefore publish its file after the close pass. When CREATE
drops its reference, the tree can be freed while the published file still
points to it.

Mark and remove the tree connection before closing its files, and serialize
both new-open and durable-reconnect volatile ID publication with that state
transition. An opener is then either published in time for the close pass
or rejected after disconnect with STATUS_NETWORK_NAME_DELETED.

Keep a tree reference while a file carries its tree pointer. This protects
asynchronous users that can defer the file's final destruction past tree
disconnect.

The close pass can race the successful FP_NEW to FP_INITED transition.
Take the opening request's file reference atomically with that transition.
This keeps the file alive until request completion even if teardown removes
the ID immediately.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99789 - block: restore the iterator when rejecting a misaligned bio
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99789
  
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 5:51 a.m. | 31 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

block: restore the iterator when rejecting a misaligned bio

bio_iov_iter_get_pages() can extract some iovecs before encountering a
misaligned one.  It releases the pages and rejects the entire bio, but
leaves the supplied iterator advanced.

An iomap direct-I/O caller may subsequently reexpand the iterator's
byte count and fall back to buffered I/O.  The reexpanded count then
includes bytes before the iterator's current segment, potentially
causing iterate_iovec() to read beyond the imported iovec array.

In a reproducer using an initial empty iovec followed by 10-byte and
1015-byte segments, writev() returned 1015 instead of 1025 and KASAN
reported an 8-byte read beyond the nine-element iovec allocation.
Saving and restoring the iterator on the rejected-bio path makes
writev() return 1025 and eliminates the KASAN report.

Restore the entire iterator rather than reverting a byte count:
advancing past an empty segment changes its position without consuming
any bytes.

Leave successful and partially accepted bio paths unchanged.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA

net/9p/usbg: remove bogus context initialization in alloc_requests

alloc_requests() initializes usb9pfs->in_req->context to point at the
struct f_usb9pfs instance itself. usb9pfs_queue_tx() later overwrites
this with the real struct p9_req_t pointer before every transmit, and
usb9pfs_tx_complete() clears it back to NULL after each completion, so
in_req->context only ever holds a valid p9_req_t once a request has
actually been queued.

usb9pfs_clear_tx(), however, can run at any time (mount close, gadget
disable) independent of whether a request was ever queued. If it runs
before the first usb9pfs_transmit(), it reads the leftover sentinel
value, type-confuses the struct f_usb9pfs pointer as a struct
p9_req_t, and both writes through it (req->t_err = -ECONNRESET) and
hands it to p9_client_cb(), which manipulates req->wq and req->refcount
at bogus offsets inside f_usb9pfs. This reliably corrupts memory or
panics whenever the transport is torn down before any 9p request has
been transmitted, e.g. mounting and immediately unmounting, or a cable
disconnect racing the very first request.

usb9pfs->out_req->context is set the same way but is never read by
this transport (usb9pfs_rx_complete() identifies the instance via
ep->driver_data instead), so it serves no purpose either.

Both endpoints' ->driver_data are already set to usb9pfs in
enable_endpoint(), which is what the completion handlers actually use
to recover the f_usb9pfs instance. Just drop the leftover
->context assignments; usb_ep_alloc_request()/alloc_ep_req() already
return zeroed requests, so in_req->context correctly starts out NULL.

Description :Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. vulnerability.summary:

Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 15 minutes ago
  
Description :netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. From 0.0.20.Final until 0.0.27.Final, OHttpClientCodec in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpClientCodec.java and OHttpServerCodec in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpServerCodec.java retain the consumed outer cumulationBuffer after a valid OHTTP exchange completes, even though OHttpRequestResponseContext.destroy in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpRequestResponseContext.java releases the inner Binary HTTP cumulation and the channel remains active. A peer can complete a large request or response and leave the keep-alive connection idle, causing the client and server handlers to retain the current high-water pooled or direct buffer capacity until later inbound content replaces it or the handler is removed. Many long-lived idle connections can pin substantial memory and create availability pressure. The issue does not cause unbounded growth for repeated exchanges on a single channel. vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-53526 - Reposilite: Reflected XSS in directory listing pages (privilege escalation via token theft)
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-53526
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 9:18 p.m. | 20 minutes ago
  
Description :Reposilite is lightweight and easy-to-use repository management software dedicated to Maven-based artifacts in the JVM ecosystem. From 3.5.16 until 3.6.0, as stated by the advisory, the Maven directory-index page interpolates the request URI without HTML escaping in its title, heading, base URL, and parent-directory link. The advisory says the content-embedded ctx.uri() is percent-encoded, preventing tag injection, but that a single quote passes through and breaks the quoted Parent-Directory link; it also says Location.of strips single quotes, so the reachability of the described quote-based trigger remains unresolved. The listing shares the Admin UI origin and does not set the sandbox Content-Security-Policy used for artifact and Javadoc responses, so the reported script execution could access a user's local-storage token. A manager token could enable full instance compromise. The advisory reports version 3.6.0 as fixed.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-104199 - aMQTT: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity and Uncontrolled Resource Consumption and Improper Input Validation
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-104199
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 7:57 p.m. | 26 minutes ago
  
Description :aMQTT is an open source MQTT broker and client. From 0.11.0 until 0.11.4, add_subscription() in amqtt/broker.py accepts malformed single-level + wildcard placement because it checks substrings instead of validating each slash-delimited level. The _matches() function converts each + into a greedy regular-expression fragment and evaluates it with re.fullmatch(), allowing a filter containing many adjacent + characters to trigger catastrophic backtracking when compared with a topic that partially matches but ultimately fails. Because matching runs synchronously in _run_broadcast(), one subscription followed by a publish can block the broker event loop, stopping message delivery and new connection processing until restart. Anonymous clients can trigger the issue with the default configuration. Any authenticated client permitted to create arbitrary subscriptions and publish messages may still exploit it when authentication is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.4.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-127060 - @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to prefix escape via semicolon path-parameter dot-segments
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-127060
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 6:18 p.m. | 13 minutes ago
  
Description :@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions before 11.6.10, it rejects destinations containing parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the rewrite-prefix containment check also passes. Servlet containers such as Apache Tomcat and Jetty strip semicolon path parameters from each segment before resolving dot-segments, so a request routed through the configured prefix is rewritten and reaches the upstream where it resolves above the intended subtree, escaping the path the proxy is meant to expose and, on some containers, crossing application contexts. Both the HTTP and WebSocket proxy paths are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99563 - smb: smbdirect: release failed pending sockets of a listener
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99563
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:18 p.m. | 18 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: smbdirect: release failed pending sockets of a listener

A child of a listener only left the listen.pending or listen.ready
list via smbdirect_socket_accept() or when the listener was
destroyed. So every connection that failed before it was accepted
(negotiate timeout, peer disconnect, invalid negotiate request, ...)
stayed on the list and counted against the backlog until the listener
was destroyed. After about backlog (10 for ksmbd) such connections
smbdirect_listen_connect_request() rejected every new connection with
-EBUSY, so an unauthenticated peer was able to permanently stop
ksmbd from accepting SMB-Direct connections.

Now a failed child moves itself to a new listen.orphaned list at the
end of smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work(), after the disconnect was
started, and queues listen.purge_orphaned_work, which releases it
with smbdirect_socket_release(), without holding the listener's
rdma_lock_handler() lock, in the same way smbdirect_socket_destroy()
does for the remaining children. Orphaned sockets still count against
the backlog until they are released.

sc->accept.listener is now only changed under listener->listen.lock
and whoever clears it is responsible for releasing the socket:
smbdirect_socket_accept(), purge_orphaned_work or the destroy of the
listener.

In order to make that work:

- a struct smbdirect_socket that is a listener is now freed via
  kfree_rcu(), so that a child can dereference sc->accept.listener
  under rcu_read_lock(), even if the listener is released concurrently.

- smbdirect_listen_connect_request() adds nsc to the listen.pending
  list and sets nsc->accept.listener before it calls
  smbdirect_accept_connect_request(), and always returns 0 so the
  rdma_cm core keeps the connection id and nsc owns it. On a non-zero
  return it schedules nsc's teardown with

Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:18 p.m. | 18 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: smbdirect: release failed pending sockets of a listener

A child of a listener only left the listen.pending or listen.ready
list via smbdirect_socket_accept() or when the listener was
destroyed. So every connection that failed before it was accepted
(negotiate timeout, peer disconnect, invalid negotiate request, ...)
stayed on the list and counted against the backlog until the listener
was destroyed. After about backlog (10 for ksmbd) such connections

ksmbd from accepting SMB-Direct connections.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99562 - ksmbd: reject FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA on a directory handle
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99562
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:18 p.m. | 18 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: reject FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA on a directory handle

An authenticated client with a writable tree connection can open a
directory with FILE_WRITE_DATA and send FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA on that
handle. The handler only checks fp->daccess & FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE, but on
a directory FILE_WRITE_DATA is the legitimate add-file right, so the
check passes. ksmbd_vfs_zero_data() then calls kernel_write() on the
directory file, which has no FMODE_WRITE, and __kernel_write_iter()
hits WARN_ON_ONCE(!(file->f_mode & FMODE_WRITE)), panicking a
panic_on_warn kernel.

Before commit 25e414db7033 ("ksmbd: report holes in allocated range
queries") the dense-file path used vfs_fallocate(), which rejects
directories with -EISDIR. The kernel_write() loop that replaced it has
no such check. Reject a directory handle in ksmbd_vfs_zero_data() before
writing, as ksmbd_vfs_write() already does for SMB2_WRITE.

  WARNING: fs/read_write.c:608 at __kernel_write_iter+0x74b/0x8c0
  Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work
  Call Trace:
   kernel_write+0x1ef/0x4d0
   ksmbd_vfs_zero_data+0x413/0x590
   smb2_ioctl+0x21fa/0x66a0
   handle_ksmbd_work+0x61b/0x1ff0

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99558 - blk-crypto: fix NULL deref and UAF in __blk_crypto_evict_key()
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99558
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:18 p.m. | 18 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

blk-crypto: fix NULL deref and UAF in __blk_crypto_evict_key()

Sashiko reported a possible NULL pointer dereference, triggered by the
following flow:

  dm-inlinecrypt ctor            # first use of the fallback
   ├─ blk_crypto_init_key()      # succeeds, ctx->key.size != 0
   ├─ blk_crypto_start_using_key()
   │   ├─ hw-wrapped key: -EOPNOTSUPP
   │   │    # profile never allocated (NULL)
   │   └─ raw key: fallback_start_using_mode()
   │      └─ blk_crypto_fallback_init() fails
   │         └─ kfree(profile)   # not NULLed
   ├─ goto bad
   └─ inlinecrypt_dtr()          # evicts whenever key.size is set
      └─ blk_crypto_evict_key()
         └─ blk_crypto_config_supported_natively() = false
            └─ blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key()
               └─ __blk_crypto_evict_key(blk_crypto_fallback_profile)
                  └─ profile->num_slots # BOOM!!!

This issue can be reproduced using the following commands:

  dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/backing bs=1M count=64
  LOOP=$(losetup -f --show /tmp/backing)
  SZ=$(blockdev --getsz $LOOP)
  KEY=$(head -c 64 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
  dmsetup create ic --table "0 $SZ inlinecrypt aes-xts-plain64 \
    $KEY 0 $LOOP 0 1 keytype:hw-wrapped"

And the following oops is triggered:

  ==================================================================
  blk-crypto: loop0: no support for wrapped keys
  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
        0xdffffc000000000b: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000058-0x000000000000005f]
  CPU: 5 UID: 0 PID: 901 Comm: dmsetup 7.3.0-rc3 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
  RIP: 0010:__blk_crypto_evict_key+0x2e/0x3b0
  Call Trace:
   blk_crypto_evict_key+0x24c/0x320
   inlinecrypt_dtr+0xf6/0x160
   inlinecrypt_ctr+0x2d3/0xbd0
   dm_table_add_target+0x661/0xf40
   table_load+0x1c4/0x490
   ctl_ioctl+0x32f/0x5f0
   dm_ctl_ioctl+0xe/0x20
  ==================================================================

dm-inlinecrypt is the only caller that can evict a key that was never
started, as fscrypt frees such a key without evicting it.

Fix this by returning early from blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key() when
tfms_inited[] is not set for the key's mode.  tfms_inited[] is only set
after blk_crypto_fallback_init() has successfully initialized the
profile, so the crash above is no longer reachable.

The bug has been latent since commit c984ff1423ae ("blk-crypto:
dynamically allocate fallback profile") was merged in v6.5, and only
became actually triggerable when commit e7f57d2c47e2 ("dm-inlinecrypt:
add target for inline block device encryption") was merged in v7.2.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99553 - nfsd: fix race between client_info_show() and free_client()
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99553
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:18 p.m. | 18 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: fix race between client_info_show() and free_client()

client_info_show() renders /proc/fs/nfsd/clients//info and walks
clp->cl_sessions under clp->cl_lock to print each session's slot
counts.  free_client() tears down the same list without taking
cl_lock, and is the only unlocked mutator of cl_sessions.  A reader
can observe a client mid-teardown because get_nfsdfs_clp() pins the
nfs4_client but not its sessions: free_client() frees every session
before calling nfsd_client_rmdir(), so an in-flight seq_file reader
can follow a list_del()'d node whose ->next now holds LIST_POISON1
and take a general protection fault:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
        0xdead00000000014c
  CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 132488 Comm: cat
  RIP: 0010:client_info_show+0x2bf/0x3d0
  RAX: dead000000000100
  Call Trace:
   seq_read_iter+0x12a/0x4b0
   seq_read+0xf1/0x130
   vfs_read+0xbf/0x350
   ksys_read+0x6f/0xf0
   do_syscall_64+0x8b/0xcb0
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x76/0x7e
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Detach cl_sessions onto a local reaplist under cl_lock, then free the
sessions after dropping the lock.  Removing entries from cl_sessions
under cl_lock matches unhash_session(), and the detach-then-reap shape
matches how __destroy_client() reaps cl_delegations.  The sessions
cannot be freed while cl_lock is held, since free_session() calls
nfsd4_del_conns(), which re-acquires it.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99552 - ocfs2/dlm: drain join handlers before releasing module text
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99552
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:18 p.m. | 18 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2/dlm: drain join handlers before releasing module text

The code for a registered DLM handler must remain resident until its
last invocation finishes. dlm_unregister_net_handlers() only removes
dlm_join_handlers from the o2net registry. o2net_handler_get() takes a
kref on the wrapper, but that reference does not pin ocfs2_dlm text.
o2net_process_message() calls nh_func after dropping o2net_handler_lock.

With CONFIG_OCFS2_FS_O2CB=m, ocfs2_dlm can be loaded independently of
ocfs2_stack_o2cb while nodemanager continues handling messages from a
configured, heartbeating peer. If no dependent module or module reference
prevents normal unload, the following ordering is possible:

  Receive worker                       Module unload
  --------------                       -------------
  o2net_handler_get()
    take wrapper kref
    drop handler lock
  
                                       dlm_exit()
                                         unregister handlers
                                       release DLM module text
  call saved nh_func
    in released module text

Use o2net_unregister_and_flush_handler_list() in the shared DLM
unregister helper. It first prevents new lookups, then waits for the
ordered o2net workqueue to drain, including a concurrent destruction of
that queue. The acquired invocation therefore finishes before dlm_exit()
returns and the loader releases the callback code. The same helper
covers partial registration and dlm_init() error unwind before module
memory is released.

Skip the drain when the private join-handler list is empty. Early
dlm_init() failures can reach this helper before any handler has been
published. Partial-registration failure also reaches it a second time
after the first call has already unregistered and drained the list.
Neither case needs to take o2net_wq_mutex or drain unrelated work.
The list is changed only by serialized module init/exit paths; a
nonempty list still uses the full unregister-and-flush helper.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99547 - thunderbolt: Do not RPM complete unrelated subtrees on unplug
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99547
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:18 p.m. | 18 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

thunderbolt: Do not RPM complete unrelated subtrees on unplug

When a Thunderbolt device is unplugged, that switch and every switch
subsequent to it on the bus device list is `complete()`d, not just its
child devices. In the case of multiple domains, it may cause, eg, an
attempt to `complete()` the uninitialized domain 1 root switch RPM
completion on unplug of a switch from domain 0 (though ordering is not
guaranteed numerically sorted).

I initially noticed this issue on a Dell XPS9720 when the system would
seem to sporadically not wake after unplugging a Thunderbolt dock. I
tried multiple kernel versions including v7.2.7 and v7.3-rc4 to see if
that resolved the issue, but the issue persisted. Eventually I found
that I could consistently generate a kernel Oops reporting a page fault
at 0xffff_ffff_ffff_fff8 on unplug from one side of the laptop and went
bug hunting. I became suspicious of the `bus_for_each_dev()` walk that I
ultimately ended up changing. To confirm this issue, I did an eBPF trace
of `bus_for_each_dev()`, `complete_rpm()`, and `complete()` while
unplugging in a variety of situations and found that an unplug from
domain 0 tries to `complete_rpm()` domain 1's switch, whose RPM
completion is not initialized and thus is holding a null wait-list
pointer, triggering the page fault.

Here are the key sections of that eBPF trace. Note that HEAD denotes the
completion's own wait-list HEAD:

```
RESCAN_ENTER domain=0

COMPLETE rescan_domain=0 target=0-1 target_domain=0
         route=0x1 parent=0-0 unplugged=1
COMPLETION done=0 head=HEAD next=HEAD prev=HEAD

BUS_WALK domain=0 start=0-1 callback=complete_rpm
CALLBACK_ENTER rescan_domain=0 dev=1-0 parent=domain1 is_switch=1

COMPLETE rescan_domain=0 target=1-0 target_domain=1
         route=0x0 parent=domain1 unplugged=0
COMPLETION done=0 head=HEAD next=0 prev=0

        complete+5
        complete_rpm+43
        bus_for_each_dev+133
        icm_free_unplugged_children+250
        icm_rescan_work+42
```

This patch gates the `complete()` on an additional condition - that the
Thunderbolt domain matches the domain of the device that was unplugged.

I only have a single system with multiple Thunderbolt domains - the Dell
XPS9720. I am consistently able to reproduce the Oops on that system.
Since running with this patch, I have not seen the Oops reoccur. I have
also tested it on a Thinkpad X1-Gen12, and that system boots and runs
well with it, but it only has a single Thunderbolt domain, so it does
not exercise the multi-domain failure case.

vulnerability.summary:

Published : 19 de Novembro de 2026 às 14:45 | 19 minutos ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mt76: mt7925: fix reset panic caused by the WM2 rx irq mask

mt7925_irq_map sets wm2_complete_mask, but mt7925_dma_layout has no

   mt7925_mac_reset_work+0x9a/0x1a0 [mt7925_common]

Remove the WM2 mask from mt7925_irq_map and from
MT7925_INT_RX_DONE_ALL.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99557 - ceph: fail readdir when the MDS reply carries no dirfrag
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99557
  
Published : 19 de Novembro de 2026 às 14:45 | 19 minutos ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: fail readdir when the MDS reply carries no dirfrag

A ceph mount oopses in ceph_readdir() when the MDS answers a READDIR
request with a reply whose extra blob is empty.  parse_reply_info()
skips reply blobs whose length is zero, so parse_reply_info_readdir()
never runs, r_reply_info.dir_dir stays NULL, and the reply still
parses as successful.  ceph_mdsc_do_request() returns 0 and
ceph_readdir() then reads rinfo->dir_dir->frag with no NULL check:

	/* extra */
	ceph_decode_32_safe(&p, end, len, bad);
	if (len > 0) {
		...
		err = parse_reply_info_extra(&p, p + len, req, features, s);
		...
	}

The oops on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820, one getdents64(2) on the
mount root after an ms_mode=legacy mount, trimmed:

BUG: KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000000-0x0000000000000007]
Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000000: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 266 Comm: ls Tainted: G                 N  7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:ceph_readdir+0xbff/0x3ea0
Call Trace:
 
 ? __pfx_ceph_readdir+0x10/0x10
 wrap_directory_iterator+0xa2/0xe0
 iterate_dir+0x1da/0x5d0
 __x64_sys_getdents64+0x13b/0x2a0
 do_syscall_64+0xdd/0x4a0
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
 

The unconditional frag read came in with 81c6aea5275ea ("ceph: handle
frag mismatch between readdir request and reply"), so the bug is old.

Treat a reply with no dirfrag as a protocol violation: warn once,
drop the request and return -EIO, the same way ceph_readdir() already
handles the two malformed-reply cases later in the function.

Tested on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 (KASAN).  Unpatched, the
getdents64(2) above takes the machine down (oops=panic) on the first
READDIR reply.  With the patch it warns once and getdents64(2)
returns -EIO, no oops, no hang.  A conformant reply for an empty
directory — dirfrag present, zero entries, FRAG_END|FRAG_COMPLETE —
still lists "." and ".." and returns EOF on both kernels, so normal
readdir behavior is unchanged.  The oops is still present in
v7.3-rc5 (72d3fcf802c45).
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99421 - ovl: always encode the origin fh when index is enabled
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99421
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 2:40 p.m. | 12 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: always encode the origin fh when index is enabled

On an overlay with index=on,nfs_export=on, copy up of a directory
crashes the kernel once an LSM has started to deny CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH
to the mounter, the task that mounted the overlay. The mount and the LSM
policy change require root. After that, any user who can write to a
directory that exists only in a lower layer triggers the oops by doing
so.

Before a file or directory that exists only in a lower layer is changed
for the first time, overlayfs copies it to the writable upper layer.
This is called copy up.

On copy up, ovl_get_origin_fh() encodes the file handle of the lower
inode, called the origin. It returns NULL if ovl_can_decode_fh() says
that the lower filesystem cannot decode handles. Whether the callers can
handle NULL depends on the index option:

- Without an index, NULL is fine: the callers store an empty origin
  xattr.
- With index enabled, overlayfs keeps entries for copied up inodes in an
  internal index directory. The name of an index entry is derived from
  the handle, so ovl_get_origin_fh() must return a handle or an error.

The mount only enables the index if ovl_can_decode_fh() succeeds for all
layers, but the result can change later. The function checks the export
operations of the filesystem and capable(CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH). Copy up
runs with the mounter's credentials, and an LSM can start to deny the
capability to those credentials after the mount. ovl_get_origin_fh()
then returns NULL with index enabled.

This goes wrong in two callers:

- With nfs_export=on, copy up of a directory creates an index entry for
  the directory. ovl_create_index() passes the NULL handle to
  ovl_get_index_name_fh(), which dereferences it.
- If the result changes while mount(2) is still running,
  ovl_get_indexdir() passes a NULL from ovl_get_origin_fh() to
  ovl_verify_set_fh() in the same way.

Before the commit in the Fixes tag, these two callers encoded the handle
themselves, without consulting ovl_can_decode_fh().

Reproduced with a BPF LSM program that started to deny the capability
after the mount. An unprivileged touch in a directory that had not been
copied up yet oopsed in ovl_get_index_name_fh(). With this patch the
touch succeeds and the directory gets its index entry.

Fix this by calling ovl_can_decode_fh() in ovl_get_origin_fh() only when
index is disabled.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99412 - xfs: avoid cross-rtgroup reaping after a repair
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99412
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 2:40 p.m. | 12 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: avoid cross-rtgroup reaping after a repair

LOLLM notices that the extents stored in a xrtb_bitmap (aka xfs_rtblock
bitmap) can span multiple rtgroups due to two circumstances.  The first
is that the size of an rtgroup is an exact power of two, which means
that rtgroups are adjacent in the segmented xfs_rtblock_t address space.
This is fairly common to reduce the amount of multiplication and
division needed to handle space on the rt volume.

The second is that (unlike in the original rtgroups design), rtgroups do
not have fixed-location metadata like AGs do, which means that there's
nothing to force a break between rtgroups.

Therefore, we must loop through the rtgroups in xreap_rtmeta_extent to
avoid running off the end of an rtgroup while reaping.

Description :In Eclipse Ditto versions 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the resolved policy view (`GET /api/2/policies/{policyId}?policy-view=resolved`) does not restrict merged policy content to what the caller may read in the policy it originates from. vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133188 - MISP Protected Event Signature Bypass via Whitespace Injection in JSON Keys and Identifiers
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133188
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 2:32 p.m. | 20 minutes ago
  
Description :MISP contains a vulnerability in the cryptographic signature verification of protected events. When a MISP instance signs a protected event for synchronization, it strips all whitespace from the JSON body before computing the PGP signature (preg_replace("/\s+/", "", $data)). The receiving instance performs the same whitespace-stripping before verification. Because the signature covers only the whitespace-free representation, a network relay positioned between two MISP instances can insert whitespace characters into JSON object keys (effectively renaming fields) or into identifier values such as UUIDs, timestamps, and distribution fields without invalidating the signature. The receiving instance accepts the modified event as authentic.

The vulnerability affects the protected event synchronization path: event creation (EventsController::add), event editing (EventsController::edit), event viewing (EventsController::view1), and server-to-server pull synchronization (ServerSyncTool, Server model). An attacker with a network position to intercept and modify traffic between MISP instances can alter the semantic content of protected events while the PGP signature still validates, undermining the integrity guarantees that protected events are designed to provide.

The fix introduces two complementary mechanisms. First, a post-verification scan rejects any received body that contains whitespace in JSON keys (except under Galaxy cluster 'meta' keys) or in identifier-like values (uuid, id, timestamp, distribution, date). Second, a new exact-byte signature scheme (x-pgp-signature-v2) signs the body as transmitted, without whitespace normalization. MISP 3.0 and later peers exchange this exact-byte signature; older peers retain the legacy whitespace-stripped signature. A signature_version field is embedded in protected events so that a 3.0 receiver refuses a body carrying that marker if only the legacy signature is present. Both mechanisms together close the whitespace-injection vector while preserving backward compatibility with pre-3.0 instances.
  
Severity: 6.9 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99320 - ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc()
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99320
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 9:18 a.m. | 1 hour, 13 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc()

rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the skb to
l3mdev_ip6_out(). The VRF output path may replace skb->dst and release
the original route, leaving the cached pointer stale.

The function later dereferences that pointer for statistics accounting
and as the output device passed to NF_HOOK(). Its RCU read-side critical
section starts after l3mdev_ip6_out(), so it cannot prevent the old route
from being reclaimed in between.

Reload the route from the current skb destination after
l3mdev_ip6_out() returns.

KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free in rawv6_sendmsg(), with the route
allocated by ip6_dst_alloc(), freed by dst_destroy() from rcu_core(), and
the related RCU callback queued from vrf_l3_out().
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the skb to
l3mdev_ip6_out(). The VRF output path may replace skb->dst and release
the original route, leaving the cached pointer stale.

The function later dereferences that pointer for statistics accounting
and as the output device passed to NF_HOOK(). Its RCU read-side critical
section starts after l3mdev_ip6_out(), so it cannot prevent the old route
from being reclaimed in between.

Reload the route from the current skb destination after
l3mdev_ip6_out() returns.

KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free in rawv6_sendmsg(), with the route
allocated by ip6_dst_alloc(), freed by dst_destroy() from rcu_core(), and
the related RCU callback queued from vrf_l3_out().

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-117678 - idna: punycode labels are decoded before the 63-octet length check, so a long xn-- label causes super-linear CPU use
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-117678
  
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 5:36 a.m. | 38 minutes ago
  
Description :Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in benoitc idna allows an attacker who controls a hostname passed to the library to exhaust CPU via an over-long xn-- label. idna:ulabel/1 in src/idna.erl hands every ASCII label that starts with xn-- to punycode:decode/1 without applying check_label_length/1, the 63-octet DNS label limit. punycode:decode/1 in src/punycode.erl builds its output with list appends in insert/4, so its cost grows super-linearly with the label length. A label of a few kilobytes keeps a scheduler busy for seconds to minutes before the label is rejected as invalid punycode.

Every decode entry point reaches this path: decode/1, decode/2, to_unicode/1 and from_ascii/1. The encode path reaches it as well, because alabel/1 calls ulabel/1 on an ASCII xn-- label before its own length check, so encode/1, encode/2 and to_ascii/1 are affected for such input.

This issue affects idna: from 0.5.0 before 8.0.0.
  
Severity: 6.9 | MEDIUM

Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 11:17 p.m. | 13 minutes ago
  
Description :Mareforma is a local verification layer for AI-assisted research. From 0.3.0 until 0.3.8, verify_bundle in mareforma/export_bundle.py validates the outer DSSE envelope and exporter-signed subject digests, but JSONLDExporter._claim_node in mareforma/exporters/jsonld.py supplies no signatureBundle for individual claims. vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-132644 - MISP Galaxy Cluster Import Authorization Bypass Allows Cross-Organization Cluster Takeover
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-132644
  
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 10:17 p.m. | 13 minutes ago
  
Description :MISP contains an authorization flaw in the GalaxyCluster model's captureCluster() function, which handles the import and synchronization of Galaxy Clusters. Prior to the fix, any authenticated user holding the galaxy editor role could replace an existing locked Galaxy Cluster by supplying its UUID in an import request, regardless of which organization owned the cluster. The function unconditionally called captureOrganisationAndSG() before the save operation, overwriting the cluster's org_id and orgc_id fields with the importing user's organization, effectively transferring ownership of the cluster to the attacker's organization. Additionally, the save operation was not restricted to a specific set of fields, allowing arbitrary field modification.

The vulnerable behavior required the attacker to possess a valid MISP account with the perm_galaxy_editor role and to know or discover the UUID of a target cluster belonging to another organization. No site-admin or owner-organization privilege was enforced for the update path. The result was that a low-privilege galaxy editor in one organization could modify the content (value, description, distribution, etc.) of clusters owned by other organizations and seize ownership, corrupting the integrity of shared threat-intelligence data across the MISP instance.

The vulnerability was reported by ENISA and CERT.pl. The fix introduces an explicit authorization gate that restricts cluster updates to the owner organization, a sync user who can see the cluster via sharing-group rules, or a site administrator, and enforces a field allow-list that excludes org_id and orgc_id from update writes, preserving original ownership.
  
Severity: 6.3 | MEDIUM

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-55171 - Open OnDemand: Predictable OIDCCryptoPassphrase default + ood-ansible variable mismatch enables session forgery
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-55171
  
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 9:06 p.m. | 20 minutes ago
  
Description :Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal. Prior to Open OnDemand 4.1.6 and 4.2.3, and prior to ood-ansible 4.2.1, the portal generator defaults OIDCCryptoPassphrase to SHA1(servername), and the templates/ood_portal.yml.j2 role checks a different variable from the documented passphrase setting. Administrators who set ood_oidc_crypto_passphrase can therefore believe a strong secret is configured while the deployment continues to use an attacker-derivable value. In OIDCSessionType client-cookie deployments, an unauthenticated remote attacker can derive the encryption key and forge a mod_auth_openidc_session cookie for another user, while server-cache deployments permit lower-impact tampering with protected OIDC state and nonce cookies. This issue is fixed in Open OnDemand versions 4.1.6 and 4.2.3 and ood-ansible version 4.2.1.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-132642 - MISP Tag Endpoints Bypass ACL Visibility, Allowing Unauthorized Tag Modification and Enumeration on Hidden Events
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-132642
  
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 9:04 p.m. | 21 minutes ago
  
Description :MISP contains an access control flaw in its tag management endpoints: events/addTag (single and bulk), events/removeTag, and attributes/removeTag. These endpoints loaded their target event or attribute using an unscoped database query (recursive = -1) that did not apply the calling user's ACL visibility rules. As a result, two distinct security issues existed: (1) Information disclosure: the removeTag endpoint returned different responses depending on whether a given tag was present on a hidden event, allowing an authenticated user to enumerate which tags were applied to events they had no visibility into. (2) Unauthorized modification: users belonging to the host organisation, who are permitted to set local tags on records they can see, could add or remove local tags on events and attributes they could not see, because the canModifyTag ACL check operated on the unscoped object without first verifying the caller's visibility. The fix replaces the unscoped find() calls with ACL-aware fetch methods (fetchSimpleEvent and fetchAttributeSimple) that apply the user's visibility before the object is returned, and adds an explicit empty-object check in removeTag so that a hidden event responds identically to a non-existent one. Affected components include the EventsController (addTag, removeTag), the AttributesController (removeTag), and the ACLComponent (canModifyTag). The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with at least the tagger role (perm_tagger) or host-organisation membership.
  
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-63129 - mssql-mcp-core: SQL injection in mssql-mcp write tools via unparameterized table names and WHERE clauses
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-63129
  
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:19 p.m. | 12 minutes ago
  
Description :mssql-mcp-core is the shared library that powers MSSQL MCP servers. Prior to core and server 0.6.0 and reader and writer 0.5.0, multiple database tools interpolate caller-controlled identifiers and predicates into T-SQL batches passed to Request.query() while parameterizing only data values. update_data, delete_data, insert_data, execute_transaction, create_table, create_index, and drop_table accept unsafe tableName, column, index, schema, or free-form whereClause input, while reader-tier list_databases interpolates stateFilter without runtime allowlist enforcement. Row-count and preview queries execute before confirmUpdate or confirmDelete, allowing malicious arguments to bypass confirmation and maxRows controls and execute stacked DDL or DML, read or destroy data, and potentially run operating-system commands when the SQL login is privileged and xp_cmdshell is enabled. This issue is fixed in core and server version 0.6.0 and reader and writer version 0.5.0.
